title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: LOU'S NEW BOSS
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Lou Brannigan, a bus mechanic in Lowell, Massachusetts.
For thirty-one years, Lou fixed city buses with a wrench and a clipboard.
Then he got a new boss. She was twenty-seven. And she had a tablet.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE NEW BOSS
segments.quote: The old believe everything; the middle-aged suspect everything; the young know everything.
segments.author: Oscar Wilde
lines: On a Monday, Taylor Nguyen said, We're going paperless.
Lou looked at his clipboard like she'd insulted his dog.
That night, his wife Deb read him a line from Oscar Wilde:
The old believe everything; the middle-aged suspect everything; the young know everything.
Lou was the middle one. So he gave Taylor one week before he grumbled.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE TABLET
segments.quote: Personally, I am always ready to learn, although I do not always like being taught.
segments.author: Winston Churchill
lines: At training class, Lou poked the screen like it owed him money.
He almost walked out. Then he saw a Winston Churchill poster in the break room:
Personally, I am always ready to learn, although I do not always like being taught.
So he stayed, and took notes. On paper.
By Friday, the tablet told him which brakes were wearing out.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE OLD WAY
segments.quote: Not everything that is faced can be changed; but nothing can be changed until it is faced.
segments.author: James Baldwin
lines: Taylor asked why so many buses broke down in winter. Lou said, That's just how it is.
She had a line from the writer James Baldwin taped to her desk:
Not everything that is faced can be changed; but nothing can be changed until it is faced.
So Lou faced it. Old heater hoses were cracking. Now he swaps them every fall.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE QUESTION
segments.quote: The important thing is not to stop questioning. Curiosity has its own reason for existence.
segments.author: Albert Einstein
lines: One morning, bus fourteen made a noise like a goose in a blender.
Taylor was afraid to ask a dumb question in front of the crew.
Lou remembered what Albert Einstein told a magazine reporter:
The important thing is not to stop questioning. Curiosity has its own reason for existence.
So Lou said, Ask me anything. Question nineteen found a loose fan belt.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE BLIZZARD
segments.quote: Tradition is a guide and not a jailer.
segments.author: W. Somerset Maugham
lines: In February, a snowstorm buried Lowell. Half the crew was snowed in.
Lou wanted to check every bus the old way. The tablet said six were in trouble first.
He thought of the novelist Somerset Maugham:
Tradition is a guide and not a jailer.
So he used his ears and her screen. Every route ran until sunrise.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE TEACHER
segments.quote: Leadership and learning are indispensable to each other.
segments.author: John F. Kennedy
lines: In spring, Taylor needed someone to train new mechanics. She picked Lou.
He said, Me? I type with one finger. She showed him a line John F. Kennedy wrote:
Leadership and learning are indispensable to each other.
Now Lou teaches wrenches, Taylor teaches screens, and every Friday he teaches her one old trick.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Wait before you grumble. Stay for the lesson. Face it. Ask. Keep the good old ways. Lead and learn.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Wait before you grumble. Stay for the lesson. Face it. Ask. Keep the good old ways. Lead and learn.
Me? I learned to text. My grandson says I type like a woodpecker.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
